picks.title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap
picks.excerpt: Lightroom for iOS, iPadOS and Android adds a one-tap generative-AI Open Eyes fix that matches lighting and pose using other shots of the same person; free users get limited tries.
picks.rationale: A new one-tap generative fix in Lightroom mobile that photographers and image-makers can use right away. It is a different feature from the 9/28 Lightroom-in-Gemini story and the 10/05 Prompt to Edit story.

picks.title: ChatGPT Slides lets users create, edit and present decks without leaving ChatGPT
picks.excerpt: OpenAI's new ChatGPT Slides turns conversations, uploaded files, outlines or a sample deck into an editable presentation, generating custom images and refining text, visuals and charts, with live team editing and PowerPoint export.
picks.rationale: A new OpenAI deck-building product with live co-editing and PowerPoint export, which changes how decks get made. It is a different product from yesterday's Gemini Notebook slides card.

picks.title: Neural Concept launches MCP to help AI agents operate commercial CAD tools
picks.excerpt: Neural Concept's Model Context Protocol Bridge lets AI agents drive commercial CAD and simulation tools, automating geometry cleanup and meshing steps in product design cycles.
picks.rationale: A new MCP bridge from Neural Concept that lets agents drive commercial CAD and simulation tools. It is a separate vendor and release from the 9/24 Multiphysics MCP and 10/03 ClassCAD stories.

picks.title: DxO ViewPoint 6 introduces AI masking, but maintains that no AI image generation takes place
picks.excerpt: DxO's perspective/geometry-correction tool ViewPoint 6 adds AI masking while stressing it does no generative image creation.
picks.rationale: A new version release: AI masking arrives in DxO's perspective-correction tool, with no generative content, which matters to architecture and product photographers who must avoid generated pixels.

picks.title: Human attention is the new old bottleneck. We have to design for it even more.
picks.excerpt: Reading Anthropic's Oct 16 study (agents now log six hours for every human hour), the piece argues designers' job shifts to building judgement systems for what deserves human attention.
picks.rationale: A design-practice read of fresh Anthropic data (six agent hours per human hour) that reframes the designer's job as deciding what deserves human attention. No earlier design card covers this study.
